content:
Apple today launched the latest Mac mini and Mac Studio models, and alongside the new product releases, several Magic Keyboard accessories under the company have also received minor updates.

The latest Magic Keyboard removes text labels on the keys, replacing them with icons.

Apple's Mac mini and Mac Studio are equipped with the more powerful next-generation chips, such as the M6 and the high-end M5 Ultra, delivering significant performance improvements.

The latest models are now available for pre-order: pre-order the Mac mini here, pre-order the Mac Studio here.

In addition to the desktop computer upgrades, Apple has also updated the Magic Keyboard lineup, with the new models featuring a subtle change.

The latest Magic Keyboard has removed text labels from many of the keys, replacing them with symbolic icons.

Apple adopted the same approach earlier this year with the MacBook Neo, MacBook Air, and MacBook Pro, and now the Magic Keyboard has followed suit with this change.

This change applies to all new Magic Keyboard models:

  • Magic Keyboard: US$99
  • Magic Keyboard with Touch ID: US$149
  • Magic Keyboard with Touch ID and Numeric Keypad: US$179

Frequently used keys such as Tab, Caps Lock, Return, Shift, and Delete have been changed from text to icons only; and on the extended models with a numeric keypad, keys such as Home, Page Up, and Page Down have also been given brand-new icons, replacing the original text labels.

Apart from the switch to symbolic icons, the new Magic Keyboard looks largely the same as the previous generation, still supporting USB-C, with features and layout remaining unchanged.

If you wish to order the new Magic Keyboard through Amazon rather than from Apple, you can purchase it here: Magic Keyboard, version with Touch ID, version with Touch ID and Numeric Keypad (black).

What are your thoughts on the design change from text labels to icons on the keys? Feel free to share with us in the comments section.
